---
title: RedisDriver
description: "Redis cache driver using php-redis extension with lazy connection, SCAN-based flush, and tag support."
---

<ApiBadge type="driver" />
<ApiBadge type="cache" />
<ApiBadge type="redis" />
<ApiBadge type="lazy-connection" />
<ApiBadge type="tag-support" />

`Skim\Cache\RedisDriver` is the production cache backend. It uses the php-redis extension (not Predis) for 5-10x better performance. Connection is lazy — the socket opens on first operation. Prefix-based flush uses SCAN to avoid blocking Redis. Tags are supported via Redis sets through `tags()`.

```txt
Symbol: Skim\Cache\RedisDriver
Source: src/Cache/RedisDriver.php
Lifecycle: lazy connection on first operation, reused for process lifetime
Fallback: FileDriver when Redis is unreachable
```

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
$driver = new RedisDriver(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379, prefix: 'skim_');
$driver->set('user:1', $data, 3600);
```
</CodeExample>

<WarningBox>

flushAll() issues FLUSHDB which destroys ALL data in the selected Redis database, not just cache keys

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

Prefer flush('prefix:') in production

</WarningBox>

## Architecture

The driver prefixes all keys with the configured prefix (default 'skim_') to namespace cache entries within a shared Redis instance. SCAN-based flush avoids the KEYS command which blocks the Redis event loop on large datasets.

<NoteBox>

Why php-redis over Predis: extension is 5-10x faster, no Composer dependency. Tags use Redis sets: tag→[key1, key2, ...] — flush by tag deletes all member keys.

</NoteBox>

## Read API

<ApiMethod name="get">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function get(string $key, mixed $default = null): mixed
```

</ApiSignature>

Reads the prefixed key from Redis, unserializes the value, and returns it or $default on miss/deserialization failure.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to read.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$default" type="mixed">

Fallback returned on miss.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="has">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function has(string $key): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Checks key existence via Redis EXISTS command.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to test.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

## Write API

<ApiMethod name="set">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function set(string $key, mixed $value, ?int $ttl = null): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Serializes the value and writes to Redis using SETEX (with TTL) or SET (without TTL).

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Cache key to write.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$value" type="mixed" required>

Payload to persist.

</ApiParam>

<ApiParam name="$ttl" type="?int">

TTL in seconds, or null for no expiry.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="delete">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function delete(string $key): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Deletes the prefixed key via Redis DEL command.

<ApiParam name="$key" type="string" required>

Exact cache key to remove.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

## Invalidation

<ApiMethod name="flush">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function flush(string $prefix): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Uses SCAN to find matching keys in batches of 100, then DEL to remove them. Avoids KEYS which blocks Redis.

<ApiParam name="$prefix" type="string" required>

Key prefix to match.

</ApiParam>

</ApiMethod>

<ApiMethod name="flushAll">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function flushAll(): bool
```

</ApiSignature>

Issues FLUSHDB on the selected Redis database, destroying all data in that database.

<WarningBox>

FLUSHDB destroys ALL data in the selected database, not just cache keys

</WarningBox>

<WarningBox>

Prefer flush('prefix:') in production

</WarningBox>

</ApiMethod>

## Tag Operations

<ApiMethod name="tags">

<ApiSignature>

```php
public function tags(array $tags): TaggedRedisDriver
```

</ApiSignature>

Returns a tag-scoped proxy that tracks key membership in Redis sets and supports grouped invalidation.

<ApiParam name="$tags" type="array" required>

Tag identifiers for grouped operations.

</ApiParam>

<CodeExample label="Basic usage" source="llm-generated">
```php
$driver->tags(['users'])->set('user:42', $data, 3600);
$driver->tags(['users'])->flush(); // Removes all keys tagged 'users'
```
</CodeExample>

</ApiMethod>
